title: Tate twists are well defined and locally free of rank one
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\cO_E$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ containing $E$. Let $X$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let $\mu_{\ell^n,X}$ be the sheaf of
$\ell^n$th roots of unity [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], with transition maps
$\mu_{\ell^{n+1},X}	o\mu_{\ell^n,X}$, $u\mapsto u^\ell$. For every finite commutative ring $A$ and integer $r\geq1$ with $\ell^rA=0$, write $A_X$ for its constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Interpret the coefficient objects and twists for $\cO_E$, $E$, and $\Qlb$ using [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

1. There is a pro-étale cover $\widetilde X	o X$ and a compatible system
   $(\zeta_n)_{n\ge1}$, $\zeta_n\in\mu_{\ell^n,X}(\widetilde X)$, $\zeta_{n+1}^\ell=\zeta_n$,
   such that each $\zeta_n$ generates: $(\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_{\widetilde X}	o\mu_{\ell^n,\widetilde X}$,
   $a\mapsto\zeta_n^a$, is an isomorphism.
2. For $r'\ge r$, the Kummer map
   $\mu_{\ell^{r'},X}	o\mu_{\ell^r,X}$, $u\mapsto u^{\ell^{r'-r}}$, induces an isomorphism
   $\mu_{\ell^{r'},X}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^{r'}}A_X\cong\mu_{\ell^r,X}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}A_X$;
   so $A_X(1)$ is independent of $r$ up to canonical isomorphism.
3. For $\Lambda\in\{A,\cO_E,E,\Qlb\}$, the sheaf $\Lambda_X(1)$ is an invertible
   $\Lambda_X$-module: on $\widetilde X$ it is isomorphic to $\Lambda_{\widetilde X}$. Hence
   so are $\Lambda_X(d)$ and $\Lambda_X(-d)$ for $d\ge0$, and
   $\Lambda_X(d)\otimes\Lambda_X(-d)\cong\Lambda_X$. The functor $K\mapsto K(d)$ is an autoequivalence, with inverse $K\mapsto K(-d)$, on each coefficient category defined in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]: $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ and the bounded constructible categories for $\cO_E$, $E$, and $\Qlb$.

proof.text: (1) By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] (2), after a pro-étale cover \widetilde X\to X the inverse-limit Tate line \mathbf Z_\ell(1) is identified with the completed constant line \widehat{\mathbf Z}_\ell. Reducing the image of its section $1$ modulo \ell^n through the canonical quotient isomorphism in that clause gives \zeta_n\in\mu_{\ell^n,X}(\widetilde X). The quotient maps send \zeta_{n+1}$ to \zeta_n$, hence \zeta_{n+1}^\ell=\zeta_n$; and the image of $1$ identifies $(\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_{\widetilde X}$ with \mu_{\ell^n,\widetilde X}. Thus this one cover and the resulting compatible generators prove (1).

(2) On the cover from (1), use the generators \zeta_{r'} and \zeta_r=\zeta_{r'}^{\ell^{r'-r}}. Both tensor products are thereby identified with the constant sheaf $A_{\widetilde X}$, and the displayed Kummer map is the identity under these identifications. Isomorphisms of sheaves are local for the pro-étale topology, so the map is an isomorphism on $X$. This proves that the finite twist is independent of the chosen annihilating level.

For a finite ring $A$ killed by \ell^r$, (1) identifies $A_X(1)$ with the constant free rank-one $A_{\widetilde X}$ on the same cover. For \cO_E$, [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] (3) gives a pro-étale cover on which \cO_E(1)_X is free of rank one over the completed coefficient sheaf. Replace the cover from (1) by its common pro-étale refinement with this cover; the compatible generators and their quotient isomorphisms pull back, so the same symbol \widetilde X now trivializes both the root sheaves and the integral twist. The integral-limit comparison [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit] identifies the completed coefficient sheaf with the inverse limit of the finite constant levels, while [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell] identifies its localization at \ell with $E_X$ and gives flatness. Thus the local trivialization base-changes to $E_X(1)\cong E_X$. The \Qlb-object is, by [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], the compatible common-stage scalar extension of the same integral/rational object, so the same local trivialization gives \Qlb_X(1)\cong\Qlb_X. Hence every displayed $\Lambda_X(1)$ is invertible.

source.place: Proof, clause (3), finite, integral, and scalar-extension cases

proof.text: The explicit construction of the twists for all coefficients at once, including the convention $\Lambda(m)$ for $m\in\mathbf Z$, is [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Tensor powers and duals of a locally free rank-one module are locally free rank one: on a cover where the line is free, this is the corresponding calculation for a free rank-one module and its dual. The evaluation map $\Lambda_X(d)\otimes\Lambda_X(-d)\to\Lambda_X$ is therefore an isomorphism locally, hence globally. Such a line is flat, so derived tensoring with it is represented termwise by ordinary tensoring; the evaluation isomorphism gives $(K(d))(-d)\cong K$ and similarly $(K(-d))(d)\cong K$ in each coefficient category defined there, including the integral representative construction for $E$ and $\Qlb$. Thus $K\mapsto K(d)$ is an autoequivalence with inverse $K\mapsto K(-d)$.
